If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content: "71 :     public Object compute(EvalContext context) {\n72 :         return computeValue(context);\n73 :     }"

Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- What the failing test expects:
  - In ExtensionFunctionTest.testNodeSetReturn(), the XPath expression "test:nodeSet()" is evaluated and the test expects an iterator over two bean instances: list(testBean.getBeans()[0], testBean.getBeans()[1]).
  - The test harness registers the “test” namespace with TestFunctions in setUp(), so test:nodeSet() dispatches to a static function in TestFunctions that returns a node set-like result.

- How extension functions are evaluated:
  - The expression for an extension function is org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.compiler.ExtensionFunction.
  - ExtensionFunction.compute(context) delegates to computeValue(context).
  - In computeValue(EvalContext) (lines 75–92), arguments are prepared and then the matching Function is resolved and invoked:
    - It looks up the function via context.getRootContext().getFunction(functionName, parameters).
    - It then returns the result of function.invoke(context, parameters) directly, without any normalization or wrapping.

- Argument conversion vs return conversion:
  - While preparing arguments, ExtensionFunction.convert(Object) only handles the case where an argument computes to an EvalContext, in which case it replaces it with ((EvalContext) object).getValue(). For all other cases, it returns the object as-is.
  - There is no analogous conversion step for the return value of the extension function.

- The reported behavior and the likely return type:
  - The issue report states that the extension function returns a BasicNodeSet containing zero or more NodePointers.
  - That aligns with what test:nodeSet() would plausibly return: a NodeSet of pointers to the two beans.

- Where it goes wrong:
  - ExtensionFunction.computeValue returns the raw object from function.invoke. If the function returns a BasicNodeSet (implementing NodeSet), that NodeSet object is returned as a plain Object.
  - The rest of the evaluation pipeline expects node-sets to be represented in a form it can iterate (typically via an EvalContext or a recognized iterable of pointers/values). Returning a NodeSet as an opaque Object means it is not expanded into its constituent values.
  - Consequently, when the test asserts an “XPath value iterator” over "test:nodeSet()", the evaluation does not iterate over the NodeSet’s contents (the two bean pointers/values), but instead treats the NodeSet as a single scalar object or otherwise fails to produce the expected two items. This results in the assertion failure.

- Summary of root cause:
  - ExtensionFunction lacks special handling for extension functions that return a NodeSet (e.g., BasicNodeSet). It returns the NodeSet instance as-is, rather than wrapping it in an EvalContext (e.g., a NodeSetContext) or converting it into an iterator/collection of values that the engine’s iteration logic recognizes.
  - Therefore, a NodeSet returned by an extension function is not properly handled and does not behave like an XPath node-set in subsequent evaluation, causing the test testNodeSetReturn to fail.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
